panels.title: A shake of 1 mm, 6 times a second
panels.subtitle: One simulated writer (writer 0, seed 200) writes “return library books by friday”. The same hand and the same shake for every row. The trackers drive the older Rev H inner-pen model (±3 mm) in this study; the Rev J inner pen reaches further. The tremor detector needs about 4.5 s of writing before it switches the listening tracker on, so the first word looks the same in every tracker row.

panels.title: Autowrite: the pen writes a known text while you sweep
panels.subtitle: Test writer 0, seed 200: the pen knows the text “return library books by friday” and writes it in the writer's own style with 2.5 mm letters, while the hand sweeps with a 1 mm shake at 8 Hz. Autowrite is a mode you turn on.

variants.label: The hand only sweeps along the line (8.5 mm/s) with a 1 mm shake, 8 times a second. With the inner pen held still, the tip would follow this path.

metrics.name: What the hand does
metrics.text: a steady sweep plus the shake; it draws no letters

panels.title: The heel wheel leads a relaxed hand along a sentence
panels.subtitle: Test writer 0, seed 200, “a big dog dug a deep pit by the pond”. The writer relaxes and holds the pen on the paper; in lead-through, a mode you turn on, the driven heel wheel pushes the pen and the hand along the line. This study used the older Rev H inner pen for the detail; the integrated Rev J run is in the whole-pen simulation.

Words read by an AI handwriting reader (literal).
